result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md: the post-event feedback request (T+2h) with a T+24h repeat, NPS/liked/improve/topic-votes content, and the once-only broadcast-opt-in ask -- the first requirement of Phase 7, Release 1's final phase.

SCHEMA CHECK (Sec0, mandatory) -- A CHANGE IS NEEDED, unlike REQ-030's own cycle. Two additions, both stated precisely for DATA-DESIGNER's own separate artefact rather than designed here: (1) a NEW feedback table -- registration_id UNIQUE NOT NULL FK (the entire mechanism behind AC2's 'a second row fails on a database constraint, verified by a raw duplicate INSERT'), nps NOT NULL integer (recommended CHECK 0-10), liked/improve nullable text, topic_votes (shape open -- text[] recommended vs jsonb, Sec0.2), and a durable skip marker per optional column (three booleans recommended, mirroring REQ-019-schema.md's five-booleans-over-one-array precedent) -- this is what makes 'skipped, not merely not-yet-reached' a durable, resumable state, the same property REQ-019 needed for its own optional profile fields; (2) ONE new nullable column on users, broadcast_opt_in_asked_at (timestamptz), resolving design question 2 exactly: users.broadcast_opt_in alone cannot distinguish never-asked from asked-and-declined (both read false) -- the new column is the 'has this ever been asked' gate, set together with broadcast_opt_in on the SAME write, mirroring consent_pd_at/consent_pd_version's existing pairing convention (REQ-014-schema.md Sec10). Design question 2's second half (does a prior YES also block re-asking, not just a prior NO) is resolved explicitly: yes -- the gate is 'was it ever asked,' never 'did they decline,' so a single timestamp covers both answers with no separate suppression rule needed.

INTERACTION PATTERN (Sec1, design question 3) -- resolved as DB-derived resumability (REQ-019's pattern), NOT REQ-030's message-text-carrier trick, with reasoning traced explicitly: REQ-030 needed its trick because S1 blocked any write before consent AND callback_data's 64-byte cap couldn't carry three free-text fields -- neither condition holds here (every respondent is already consented and admitted+checked-in; no step needs to carry more than one small token in callback_data). A NEW wrinkle NEITHER precedent faced is named and solved: Feedback is 1:1 with Registration, not User, so the same person can have multiple concurrent feedback flows in flight (two events ending a day apart) -- a bare text listener can't tell which one a free-text reply answers. Resolved via Telegram force_reply on every free-text prompt (liked/improve/topicVotes) plus a fixed 'Feedback ref: <registrationId>' line the prompt's own text carries and the reply's reply_to_message.text is parsed back against (Sec3.1) -- disambiguation via a Telegram-held message, the same non-bot-owned-state category REQ-030 Sec1.1 already established, applied here to a different problem (identifying WHICH row, not carrying answer data). Since force_reply and an inline Skip button cannot coexist on one Telegram message (one reply_markup type per message), Skip is a typed reply keyword instead (Sec4), generalizing REQ-019's own phone-step precedent (chosen there for the identical request_contact-vs-inline-keyboard conflict) to all three optional fields rather than just one.

EXACTLY WHEN THE FEEDBACK ROW IS CREATED (Sec1.3, traced per the task's own instruction) -- on the NPS answer, and ONLY then. writeFeedbackNps performs the first and only INSERT (registration_id, nps); every subsequent optional-field write is an UPDATE only (never insert-if-absent), reachable exclusively because Sec2.2's own field-ordering rule never names liked/improve/topicVotes as the next step until nps is non-null. Skipping NPS saves nothing because there is no Skip affordance on the NPS step anywhere in this design (only 11 numbered buttons, Sec3.2) -- structural, not a rule a handler has to remember.

SCHEDULED JOBS (Sec5) -- the third and final Release-1 consumer of scheduler/runner.ts (REQ-025/026), as directed. Two new selection queries (selectRegistrationsForFeedbackRequest/-Reminder, domain/feedback.ts) mirror domain/reminders.ts's window-table style, adapted from a forward-looking (T-minus) window to a backward-looking (T-plus) one: checked_in_at IS NOT NULL is AC1's entire mechanism (admitted-but-never-checked-in never enters either candidate list); a bounded catch-up window (constant left to BACKEND-DEV to size, Sec 10 open question 3) avoids an ever-growing unbounded backward scan, justified by the same 'sendLedgeredNotification already accepts an under-sending risk, so nothing legitimate is lost by bounding it' reasoning REQ-025 Sec3.2 already established. The T+24h reminder query ADDITIONALLY excludes any registration that already has a feedback row (a stated, named design decision, Sec5.3/Sec10 open question 5, not literally forced by AC4's wording) -- reflects 'ignores the request' as 'never engaged with NPS at all.' Two distinct NotificationKinds (feedback_request already existed in the union; feedback_reminder is the one new addition) each independently governed by sendLedgeredNotification's own UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) ledger constraint is what makes AC4's T+24h-then-T+48h double-run count to exactly one reminder. Both jobs' composeMessage functions ALWAYS render the NPS prompt only (never later steps) -- traced explicitly in Sec5.4 as the reason ComposedMessage's existing type needs no force_reply variant: every force_reply prompt is sent directly by the interactive handlers via ctx.reply, never through the ledger, since there is no scheduler-driven double-send risk for a message that only ever fires synchronously in response to the respondent's own prior action.

HANDLERS (Sec6) -- three new: an NPS callback, a broadcast-ask Yes/No callback, and one generic reply-to-message text listener (never a bare message:text listener, per Sec1.2's disambiguation requirement). All three follow the identical derive-then-gate discipline already established at REQ-019 Sec4.6/REQ-030 Sec8.2-8.3, PLUS a NEW ownership check this design adds explicitly (Sec6.1 step 6, Sec6.3 step 6): a resolved registration's userId must equal the tapping/replying person's own resolved user id (S3) before any write -- refusing a forwarded or otherwise leaked button/reply tapped by someone else's Telegram account, checked before any feedback/user state is even read.

All 7 ACs mapped to concrete design elements in Sec8. 5 open questions stated explicitly in Sec10: the schema dependency itself (Sec0, blocking); topic_votes' storage shape AND whether topics should ever be tied to a real taxonomy (none exists in this codebase today, confirmed by inspecting events.agenda's own free-form JSONB shape); the CATCH_UP_WINDOW constant's size (implementation choice); whether re-answering NPS before finishing the rest of the flow should be allowed (this design allows it, via an ON CONFLICT upsert, since nothing forbids it); the T+24h reminder's already-has-a-feedback-row exclusion being this design's own reading of 'ignores,' not literally forced by AC4.

No talk/speaker question or entity anywhere in this design (AC6) -- stated as a deliberate, explicit scope boundary (Release 3, needs the Talk entity) matching the requirement text's own framing, not a silent omission.
result.next_action: Route to DATA-DESIGNER for docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md (parallel Step 1, per the REQ-014/REQ-016/REQ-019 convention for a bot requirement that adds/alters stored data) -- covering the new feedback table (registration_id UNIQUE NOT NULL, nps NOT NULL with a recommended 0-10 CHECK, liked/improve nullable text, topic_votes shape open, three optional-field skip markers) and the new users.broadcast_opt_in_asked_at nullable timestamptz column. Once that artefact lands, both this design and REQ-031-schema.md route together to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b), which cannot pass this design until the schema artefact exists (Sec0's own stated blocker).
